note: The show-repo app's own destinations: every address a reader can be sent to, what it is for, and which files render it. This is the UI layer stated as data, which the app could not say about itself before: the VIEWS table in app/index.html owns the routing (what a key does, what it stamps) and carries no label, no gloss, and no idea which code draws the screen. Read by the Activity view's Routes tab, which ranks these rows by when their files last moved and joins each to the branches touching them, and gated by tools/test/app-routes.test.mjs against the VIEWS table so a route cannot exist in one and not the other. `routes` is the word for an address, not for a toss route: docs/routes.json owns that other sense (a content type mapped to a renderer page), a different target, and the two never describe the same thing.
shellNote: The shell is every route's file: it holds the router, the header, the sidebar, and the panes' outer markup, so a commit to it touches all of them and says nothing about which. The Routes tab therefore excludes it from attribution and reports it on its own row. A route whose `files` are empty has no code of its own AT ALL and renders from an inline component in the shell; that is a fact about the app worth reading, not a gap in this file.

groups.label: Repo
groups.gloss: Reached with a repo open: the browser over one repository.

groups.label: Estate
groups.gloss: Above any repo: the constellation's own dashboard.

groups.label: Shell
groups.gloss: Addresses that are not a screen of their own.

routes.label: Overview
routes.what: A repo's front page: its README, with the repo's stats and a jump to the atlas.
routes.note: Renders from overview(), defined inline in the shell, so it has no file of its own. It used to be a three-way choice (a declared landing page, else the pages gallery, else this); the README lost that choice whenever anything else was declared, so the other two became rows of their own.

routes.note: A standing view since 2026-08-14, wherever there is a catalog; it used to appear only when a custom landing had taken the front door from it. The same inline gallery() the landing used to use.

routes.note: Assembled inline in the shell from the components the four pills reuse.

routes.label: Repos

routes.label: Stage

routes.label: Saved

routes.label: Branches

routes.label: Sessions

routes.label: Guides

routes.note: Not a screen this repo draws: the shell frames whatever page the address names.

stopNote: The nav destination a route is reached as. It exists because the router FLATTENS: six sub-tabs are addressed as their own ?view= key (Activity's five, Lists' two, Stage's two) while twelve others are addressed as ?view=<parent>&tab= (Map's eight, Project's four). Same concept, two encodings, and the reason is archaeological rather than designed: each flattened key used to BE a nav stop, and was kept when its pane moved under another so saved links keep resolving. A view key that outlived its stop is a fossil, and listing fossils at the same rank as live destinations is what made the pane read oddly. This field restores the level the router lost, and the gate holds it to estateNav, so the flattening is stated here rather than inferred. A stop owning one route is not a grouping, and the pane renders it as a plain row.
